note: Written to be spoken: one sentence or phrase per line; {"beat": s} is a deliberate pause; code is spelled the way it is said. `answer` plays after the learner answers a predict step.

lines: Data Engineering opens with five quick refreshers.
This one is Python... the parts a senior engineer leans on in code review, and the language our pipelines are written in.
All familiar? Swipe on to Git.
Here's a classic.
A function's default value is created once... when the function is defined. Not on every call.
So, what will the second call give you?
answer: Both calls share the same list... the one made when the function was defined.
The fix? Default to None, and create the list inside the function.

lines: A comprehension reads almost like a sentence.
Keep the items that pass the test... transform them... and collect the result.
The same shape builds dictionaries and sets.
And the loop variable? It stays inside.
Both of these lines compute the same sum.
But the list version builds a million items first... about forty megabytes.
The generator hands them over one at a time, in half a kilobyte.
That's how a pipeline reads files bigger than memory.
Put yield in a function, and it becomes a generator.
Each time you ask for the next value, it runs up to the next yield... hands that value back... and pauses right there, remembering everything.
Batching a stream takes just a few lines.
A with block guarantees cleanup.
When the block ends, the exit code runs... even if something blew up inside.
Files, connections, locks, transactions... they all rely on it.
With context manager, setup goes before the yield, and teardown goes in finally.
Put timed above a function, and Python replaces it with timed of that function. A new function, wrapping the old one.
Retrying, caching, timing, checking access... those are usually decorators.
Just remember to copy the original function's name across, with the wraps helper. Otherwise every log line says wrapper.
A dataclass writes the boring parts for you: the constructor, a readable printout, and equality.
Frozen makes it immutable.
And slots drops the per-instance dictionary... so millions of small records take less memory.
Last one.
This function says it takes an int.
So... what happens if you pass it a string?
answer: It simply returns the string, twice.
Python doesn't check type hints when the code runs. A type checker does.
Run one in CI, and it catches this before it ships.

lines: So... seven things to keep.
Defaults run once. Comprehensions filter, then map. Generators stream.
A with block always cleans up. Decorators wrap. Dataclasses write the boilerplate.
And hints are checked by tools, not at runtime.
Next up... Git.
